question.text:
Consider the following four compounds I, II, III, and IV.

Choose the correct statement(s).

options.text: The magnitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>pK</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></msub></math> difference between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is more than that between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>III</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>IV</mi></math>.
Resonance effect is more in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>III</mi></math> than in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>IV</mi></math>.
Steric effect makes compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>IV</mi></math> more basic than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>III</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The correct basic strength order is

(A) Kb:IV>II>∣>III;

  • IV is strongest base due to SIR effect.
  • III is weakest base due to-M group of three nitro groups present at Ortho and Para positions.
  • Il is stronger than I since III is tertiary and I primary aromatic amine.

(B) IV is found to be 40,000 times more basic than III. While I and II differ very little in basic strength.

(C,D) Due to SIR effect in IV both -NO2 and -NCH32 will be out of plane hence resonance effect is more in III than in IV.
in III than in $\mathrm{V}$.
